chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Farqad and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who both said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and with us was Rabi'ah al-Ra'i. We mentioned the merit of the Quran. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If Ibn Mas'ud does not recite according to our recitation, then he is astray.' Rabi'ah said, 'Astray?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, astray.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for us, we recite according to the recitation of Ubayy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the Imams' recitation and that of Ubayy ibn Ka'b according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt's recitation by contrasting it with that of the prominent companion Ibn Mas'ud, declaring him 'astray' if he did not follow their qira'ah. The Imam further clarifies that their specific recitation aligns with that of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, highlighting a distinct scholarly lineage and textual authority within Shia tradition. This underscores the concept of the Imams as the ultimate interpreters and preservers of the Quranic recitation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Farqad and Al Moalla Bin Khunays who both said,

‘We were both in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and with us was Rabi’e Al-Ra’iy, and we mentioned the merits of the Quran. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was so that Ibn Masoud is not reciting upon our<sup>asws</sup> recitation, so he has strayed’. So Rabi’e said, ‘Strayed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, strayed’. 
Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for us<sup>asws</sup>, so we<sup>asws</sup> are reciting it upon the recitation of my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 27. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Farqad and al-Mu’alla ibn Khunays who have said the following:

“Once we were in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and with us Rabi’ah al-Ra’y was also present. We spoke of the excellence of the Holy Quran. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘If ibn Mas’ud does not read the Holy Quran the way we read, he is straying.’ Rabi‘ah then said, ‘(Is it) straying?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, (it is) straying.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘We read the Holy Quran as my father did.’”
